videos.script: Every vector you keep costs four bytes per number, for as long as you keep it. {{bytes}} That sounds small. Then you count the rows, and the copies nobody told you about. {{rows}} This lesson weighs a vector store. You will load twenty thousand vectors into a file and into Postgres, and see the database charge more than the file. {{table}} You will build two indexes and find that each one keeps its own copy of every vector. {{copies}} Then you will shrink the vectors four ways and measure what each way costs in search quality. Some of them are nearly free. One of them costs nearly a third of the neighbours, or more. {{shrink}} You will price a change of model, in tokens, in hours and in disk. {{reindex}} You will delete half an index and watch it stay the same size, until a rebuild halves it. {{delete}} And you will put it all into one bill for two million chunks. The tokens are the cheap line. {{budget}} The storage is the one that comes back every month. {{end}}
